usageNotes: Use this to inspect what privileges a user or API token holds, either across all ACL paths or scoped to a specific path. Without `auth-id`, it returns the calling identity's own permissions; with `auth-id` specified, `Sys.Audit` on `/access` is required. Useful before performing privileged operations to confirm the caller has the necessary rights without triggering a failed request.

examples.summary: Get permissions for a specific API token scoped to the /nodes path

tips: Omit both params to quickly audit your own token's full permission map — useful when debugging 403 errors.
The `path` filter narrows results to a single ACL tree node; without it you receive the entire permission map, which can be large.
The `auth-id` format differs between users (`user@realm`) and API tokens (`user@realm!tokenid`) — the pattern enforces this distinction.
The response map keys are ACL paths (e.g. `/nodes/pve`) and values are maps of privilege name to propagate flag (1 = propagate, 0 = no propagate).
